methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $365M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Noveon Magnetics, a Series C materials-science company founded by Scott Dunn and Peter Afiuny, has raised $365M to date. The comparable universe for valuation is limited, comprising one identified private peer (Lyten) and no public comparables, reflecting the early-stage and specialized nature of frontier materials development.

The stage-progression method is the applicable triangulation approach given data constraints. Using total capital raised of $365M as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C to subsequent-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $620M. This method assumes that cumulative capital deployed and burn profiles align with historical stage-advancement patterns, though the thin comp set limits external validation of this multiplier.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $527M (low) to $714M (high), with a median of $620M. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the single private comparable, the applicability of generic stage-progression multiples to materials-science companies (which may have atypical burn and development timelines), and the absence of revenue, unit economics, or patent-portfolio data that might anchor a bottom-up approach. Any update to valuation should prioritize additional peer identification and operational metrics specific to the sector.
